help.name: The name shown in lists. Example: Service portal upgrade.
help.code: Generated on save as PRJ-000001. It is not typed in.
help.description: A short project summary. Example: Renew the customer self-service interface.
help.type: A PMO catalog classification. Example: Technical.
help.owning_unit: The unit accountable for the project, independent of HR departments. Example: Transformation office.
help.sponsor: A documentary sponsor only; choosing one does not grant project management. Use the same people picker as the manager.
help.manager: The project manager. Changing this changes who can manage this record.
help.authority: Business authority text, not technical permissions. Example: Executive committee approval in March.
help.rationale: Why the project runs now. Example: Customer satisfaction with the current portal is falling.
help.objectives: Goal, metric, and target rows. Leave a cell blank if it is not set yet. Example goal: Launch the portal.
help.objectiveGoal: What you want to achieve. Example: Reduce request time.
help.objectiveMetric: How the result is measured. Example: Average completion days.
help.objectiveTarget: The target value or unit as text. Example: Under 3 days.
help.benefits: Expected benefits, separate from objectives. Example: Save the service team 20 hours a week.
help.scope: What is in the work. Example: The web app and API.
help.exclusions: What is explicitly out. Example: The mobile app is out of this phase.
help.high_level_requirements: High-level needs, not a detailed spec. Example: National-ID sign-in.
help.deliverables: Agreed outputs. Name, description, and acceptance sit on the same row.
help.deliverableName: The deliverable name. Example: Operating guide.
help.deliverableDescription: What the deliverable includes. Example: Launch steps and the first two weeks of support.
help.acceptance: When this deliverable is accepted. Example: Operations manager sign-off. This is not project success.
help.success: How the whole project is judged successful, not one deliverable. Example: A week of stable service with no outage.
help.date_start: A calendar start date as YYYY-MM-DD with no timezone conversion.
help.date_end: A calendar end date as YYYY-MM-DD. Either date may be left empty.
help.budget_state: Unknown or estimate only. No accounting and no financial approval.
help.amount: Visible to every project reader. Zero is a valid estimate. Leave it empty when the budget is unknown.
help.currency: The company currency, read-only. It is not chosen here.
help.priority: A closed list: low, normal, high, or critical.
help.assumptions: What the plan treats as true. Example: Customer data is available before launch.
help.constraints: Limits that cannot be crossed. Example: No downtime during business hours.
help.closure: Conditions for closing the project itself, not archiving the charter. Example: Final report delivered and operations accepted.
